newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end up on continued rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end up on continued rebound.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B shares closed broadly higher on Monday on a rebound extending from Friday following recent falls brought about by Beijing's tough crackdown on excessive speculation, brokers said.
The A share index jumped 12.03 points or 2.79 percent to end at 443.12 on turnover of 8.1 billion yuan against 7.0 billion yuan last Friday.
The B share index gained 2.96 points or 2.02 percent to 149.12 on turnover of HK$65 million, compared with Friday's HK$54 million.

"Investors think the worst of the negative news has emerged and they started buying in anticipation of no further bad news at least over the short term," an analyst with Jardine Fleming Securities Ltd in Shenzhen said.
"I expect the market will continue to recover some losses later this week after the steep falls throughout most of last week," the analyst said.
"But expected gains this week are likely to be limited with the retreat of the big players," she said, referring to state banks, listed firms and state enterprises."

China confirmed last Friday that Zhou Daojiong, the chief of its top stock market watchdog China Securities Regulatory Commission had been replaced in the latest of a string of harsh measures aimed at eliminating share trading irregularities.
Industry sources have said he was removed because his efforts at reining in China's unruly stock markets had not been effective enough.
Zhou Zhengqing, chairman of the Securities Commission under the State Council, or cabinet, had taken up the additional job as head of the market watchdog.
Beijing last week also imposed tough penalities on banks, including market heavyweight Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd, and top brokerages for speculative trading.
Trading in Shenzhen Bank's A shares was suspended last Friday and is due to resume this Friday.
This came as the central government barred state banks, listed firms and state enterprises from speculative share trading and ordered them to liquidate equity positions within various time limits.

"More investors now seem to be interpreting Beijing's recent clampdown as being aimed at fostering the long-term healthy development of the market rather than just bad news for equity investors," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
The series of crackdown measures had been factored into the market, which appeared to have bottomed out temporarily according to technical charts, brokers said.
Brokers said they generally expected the A and B share markets to have more upside this week and expected B shares to continue to move closely in line with their A share counterparts.
On the B share market, toll road operator Guangdong Provincial Expressway was the best performer, surging HK$0.70 to its ten percent limit up level at HK$7.68.
Newcomer Beijing Orient Electronics was the most actively traded on volume of 3.1 million shares, adding HK$0.21 to HK$4.18.
